title: Capacity Commitment Triage: Customer SLA-to-GPU Tier Recommendation Framework
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Purpose: create a repeatable intake and triage process that maps enterprise customer throughput+SLA requirements to a recommended Reserved Capacity profile (GPU class, reserved throughput, scaling policy, and fallback strategy).

Problem statement: Sales and Solutions frequently bring requests that mix hard SLA targets, ambiguous throughput estimates, and varying cost sensitivity. We need a consistent rubric so we can: 1) give a defensible capacity recommendation, 2) surface engineering constraints early, and 3) set customer expectations for trade-offs (latency vs cost vs availability).

Goals: 
- Produce a one-page intake checklist for Sales/SEs that captures required telemetry (QPS, p99 latency goal, payload size distribution, prompt length percentiles, steady-state vs burst expectations, retention/KV-cache needs).
- Define a mapping matrix from SLA profile -> GPU class (A100, H100, L4, etc) and reservation sizing rules (tokens/sec or requests/sec tie-breakers).
- Propose default scaling policies (min reserved, burst capacity gating, cooldown windows) and a fallback order (graded model downgrades, region failover, queued requests) for enterprise SLAs.
- Deliver acceptance criteria, sample intake responses for three archetypal customers (low-latency fintech, cost-sensitive analytics, high-throughput content ingestion).

Approach: 
1) Synthesize historical onboarding data (last 18 months) to extract real-world throughput and model selection patterns. Work with ENG telemetry owners (ENG-3321) to get token/sec histograms and p99 latency vs GPU class curves.
2) Draft a rubric that translates a customer's 95%/99% latency goals and traffic profile into candidate GPU classes and a baseline reserved throughput. Include cost delta estimates for each candidate.
3) Iterate with Solutions and Sales on 3 pilot intake requests; update the rubric based on mismatch cases.
4) Bake the rubric into an intake form and a templated reply that sets expectations and next steps (PO, network setup, timeline).

Decision trade-offs to capture: 
- Single large GPU vs more smaller GPUs: trade memory limits, cold-start KV cache warming, and batching efficiency.
- Aggressive autoscale (fast ramps) increases infra cost; conservative autoscale increases risk of SLA misses. Provide SLO-aligned defaults (e.g., for p99<150ms use reserved min equal to 1.5x baseline steady-state QPS).
- Fallback behavior: earliest safe fallback should prioritize availability; propose a standard order: 1) increase model-latency budget by switching to a quantized/compatible variant, 2) route to a secondary region, 3) degrade request fidelity with structured fallback.

Deliverables: 
- Intake checklist (one-pager) + sample completed intake for three customers.
- SLA-to-GPU mapping matrix (CSV and human-readable guide).
- Recommended default scaling policy templates and a canned customer response.
- Engineering action items: telemetry gaps and required performance curves (ENG owners).

Notes: this ticket is intentionally scoped to the recommendation framework. Implementation of autoscale controls or console UI changes will be separate ENG tickets.
